articles.title: Big Bang Theory Spinoff Features Surprise Live-Action Cameos from The Flash and Mr. Freeze
articles.summary: Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails to Save the Universe featured a surprise fight between a live-action Flash and Mr. Freeze, but the show's creators originally wanted a different DC hero cameo.
body: Fans of the sci-fi comedy offshoot may have been surprised to see it dive headfirst into comic book crossover territory when Season 1 Episode 9 premiered earlier this week. The episode saw Stuart Bloom and his universe-traveling companions plopped into a Gotham City come to life, with things quickly taking a turn when none other than classic Batman villain Mr. Freeze (played here by Eric Allan Kramer) shows up.

TV show budgets aside, this is a full-on live-action take on Victor Fries that shoots killer icicles, builds giant ice walls, and even tries to kill Stuart with a giant icy bowling ball. DC fans found even more to recognize when a live-action version of Jay Garrick's Flash (played by Andy Ridings) ran in to save the day – and deliver a few one-liners.

Stuart Fails to Save the Universe packed in the references, with there even being a mention that Golden Age Flash should probably be fighting someone like Captain Cold instead of Mr. Freeze. It was enough to get tongues wagging on social media, with fans mostly just happy to see any live-action Flash for the first time since Ezra Miller played Barry Allen in 2023's universe-ending standalone film.
points: Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails to Save the Universe featured a surprise fight between a live-action Flash and Mr. Freeze, but the show's creators originally wanted a different DC hero cameo.

articles.title: The Best Pokémon Games to Start With Are Still the Classics From 20 Years Ago
articles.summary: The Pokémon franchise from Game Freak is a revolving door. Someone is always going in for the first time, while someone else is on the way out. There’s a new mainline entry or remake every few years, which keeps interest levels high. Sooner or later, most of us cave and try a Pokémon game.
body: My own entry came with Pokémon Pearl and Pokémon Diamond. Those titles arrived in Japan on Sep. 28, 2006, two decades ago. And although plenty of newer titles have come along with ambitious new twists, those classic Pokémon games are still a perfect starting point, even 20 years later.

My game of choice was Pokémon Pearl. The cover art featured Palkia, a warrior lizard with sturdy legs and an extended neck. I wasn’t completely enamored with its design, but it interested me more than Pokémon Diamond ’s Dialga, which more closely resembled a plant-eating dinosaur. I wanted the other monsters to fear my starter, not eye it as a possible addition to their lunch menu.

Besides those attractions, the games added a bunch of other new Pokémon to the mix. There were 107 new monsters in total, and players had to pick up both games if they wanted to “catch ‘em all” and complete their Pokédex. Either that, or they needed to trade with friends who owned the other version, using the Global Trade Station feature with the Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection.
points: The Pokémon franchise from Game Freak is a revolving door.

articles.title: CBS's Sleeper Hit Sitcom of the Decade Is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.summary: Countless American adaptations of British classics have fallen woefully short of the source material. Either the British humor simply doesn’t translate well because of cultural differences — which is why the U.S.
body: However, some adaptations are thoroughly enjoyable. More importantly, they respect the original premise, adapting what makes it special while adding their own twist. One such adaptation does just that — and it's now available to stream for free on Pluto TV.

Ghosts premiered in 2021 on CBS. Showrunners Joe Port and Joe Wiseman adapted the U.K. series of the same name from the BBC, bringing the original's charm to the U.S. The sitcom quickly found success, earning a second season the following January, with multiple seasons later confirmed. At the time of writing, season 6 is scheduled to debut in early 2027, with no end in sight.

Like the BBC original, Ghosts follows a young couple who believe their lives have taken a positive turn when they inherit a massive mansion from a recently deceased relative. However, what they think is a dream come true soon takes a turn for the worse when they realize the mansion they’ve inherited is riddled with ghosts.

articles.title: The Last of Us Director Apologizes to God of War Laufey Devs After Calling Recent AAA Games 'Boring'
articles.summary: The Last of Us game director Bruce Straley has apologized to the God of War Laufey team after his comments about modern AAA games brought "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention."
body: The comments in question surfaced as part of a recently published piece by Edge magazine and saw the former Naughty Dog developer tackling the state of AAA gaming and game development. Straley initially said with a laugh that he thinks "the verbs and experiences we're delivering in the triple-A space are… I wanna say boring," before bringing God of War Laufey into the equation.

"God of War Laufey, I look at that game, and every pixel is mindblowing," he said to Edge. "The amount of work and skill that's gone into every single frame… I've made those kinds of games, and I'm still blown away. But when I actually look at what you're doing in the game? I'm not excited. And that's nothing against the God of War team. Just, across the board in triple-A, it feels like there’s no opportunity to inject fresh, innovative ideas."

The Last of Us has certainly had its influence on the state of big-budget games, so it was no surprise to see social media light up with reactions to Straley's thoughts. The former Naughty Dog lead then followed up the commotion with a thread of posts on X/Twitter, taking the opportunity to elaborate on his perspective on where the industry is at and where it's heading.
points: The Last of Us game director Bruce Straley has apologized to the God of War Laufey team after his comments about modern AAA games brought "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention."

articles.title: PAX West 2026's Most Surprising Hit Was a 150-Year-Old Board Game that Combines Darts and Woodworking
articles.summary: I was dangerously late to this particular party. My editor told me that I should try to play some crokinole while I was at the Penny Arcade Expo in Seattle, as it's become popular recently, and my first reaction was that he'd just made that word up.
body: When I got to the demo room on the basement level of the Washington State Convention Center, I discovered maybe a dozen tables that were all dedicated exclusively to crokinole, played on beautiful, handmade wooden boards, and there was a crowd seated at them. It felt as if I was the only person who noticed some kind of cosmic retcon, where an unknown force had decided to re-edit the universe to account for the existence and sudden popularity of a previously unknown Canadian table game.
I know that is not what actually happened. I was just ignorant in a specific way. But it was weird.

For the benefit of others who may not know what in the hell this game is: crokinole is a head-to-head game of finger dexterity where both players compete to slide pucks into the highest-scoring areas of the board. ( Editor’s Note: I often just call the game Ping-Puck! ) It's a little bit billiards and a little bit darts and a little bit reminiscent of small children messing around on a bumper pool table. It's easy to pick up, but is an almost pure test of both geometry skills and hand-eye coordination.

articles.title: 31 Years Later, One 'Calvin and Hobbes' Line Remains The Greatest Quote In Comic Strip History
articles.summary: If you were in a position to be reading comics at the time, then Calvin and Hobbes likely found some way to crawl into your brain. At a moment when newspaper comics were beginning their headlong dive into functional irrelevance, Watterson was insistent upon keeping his work creative, fresh…
body: Last New Year's Eve marked the 30th anniversary of the ending of Bill Watterson's seminal newspaper strip Calvin and Hobbes, the impact of which is still being felt throughout Western print media to this day.

As a result, there's a non-trivial amount of Calvin and Hobbes 's weird DNA in the webcomics movement of the 2000s, in Western indie comics in general, and in fiction as a whole. Even better, Watterson chose to walk away at the height of his fame and abilities, rather than hand Calvin and Hobbes off to an anonymous imitator at his syndicate or eventually age into self-parody. Since then, Watterson has been famously reclusive, only emerging from retirement for occasional gimmicks like a stint in 2014 as an uncredited guest artist on Pearls Before Swine.

As with any daily strip, the "best" Calvin and Hobbes is largely an exercise left up to the reader. Ask any 10 fans and you're likely to get 11 answers, none of which are untrue or invalid. When we kicked the idea of this column around here at Polygon, we were no different; everyone who was willing to cite a specific favorite strip or quotation from Calvin and Hobbes brought up a different one.
points: If you were in a position to be reading comics at the time, then Calvin and Hobbes likely found some way to crawl into your brain.

articles.title: Insomniac Says Marvel's Wolverine Uses No Generative AI After Fans Spot Strange Signs in-Game
articles.summary: Insomniac Games has stepped in to confirm Marvel's Wolverine contains no generative AI after a few bizarre in-game signs raised eyebrows on social media. The hubbub surrounding the new PlayStation 5 exclusive's latest controversial moment kicked off when TikToker SmoothMango shared a video of their…
body: "Folks, that looks AI-generated," SmoothMango said. "I am trying to think of a way to describe this that is not AI generation because there's no way it's a bathroom for mutants. That looks supremely suss."

At least as it's presented here, the bathroom signs certainly seem odd. With fear surrounding AI at an all-time high, fans latched onto the clip, concerned that Insomniac had used the controversial technology to help build Marvel's Wolverine.

The glitchy bathroom signs then, of course, found their way over to X/Twitter, where user Rock Solid shared images from the video. Fans again swarmed out of fear, but Insomniac has since said its Wolverine game doesn't feature a drop of genAI.

The developer's director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, replied to the X post in question to clear the air. He said "a UV map bug" is behind the strange bathroom signs, promising that Insomniac is currently working on a fix that should address any similar instances of glitchy visuals. For those who still had question marks above their heads, Stevenson was more direct: "There are no AI-generated assets in Marvel's Wolverine."
points: Insomniac Games has stepped in to confirm Marvel's Wolverine contains no generative AI after a few bizarre in-game signs raised eyebrows on social media.

body: Between a shelf overflowing with a collection of over 100 Eevee plushies and my ongoing quest to complete an ultimate Eevee Master Set binder (collecting every single variant, promo, and English card ever printed for our favorite fluffball), this Pokémon is my number one.

articles.title: Evidence of canceled Grand Theft Auto 5 Liberty City and 'Agent Trevor' DLC, plus early version of GTA6's map surface online
articles.summary: As reported by IGN, a trove of data from Rockstar has made its way online, with the big ticket items being Grand Theft Auto 5's source code, remnants of canceled GTA5 singleplayer DLC, as well as an early version of GTA6's map that can be loaded into the prior game.
body: It's unclear how or why the data is making the rounds now, but the consensus appears to be that it was first extracted from Rockstar in the infamous 2022 Lapsus hack that revealed GTA6 to the world.

GTA YouTuber TJGM has a video and a number of posts on X covering the long-rumored Liberty City project. The gameplay in the video comes from a canceled mod, and not the leaked material. The most notable thing TJGM showed off is a map of audio loading zones contained in the leak: The demarcation for coastal ambient audio could be turned into an effective map of the multi-island city. This iteration of Liberty City would have been larger, and possessed a different layout from its most recent predecessor in GTA4.

User affmal on Twitter has been sharing screenshots and findings mostly focused on the Agent Trevor files, which appear to be more intact and substantial than the Liberty City stuff. Affmal has shared a full mission list, and has been loading map and model data into GTA5 to explore. The coolest thing affmal has shown off, for my money, is an underwater base map like something out of Deus Ex.

articles.title: An ambitious fanmade expansion for Baldur's Gate 3 is out after almost two years in development
articles.summary: Baldur's Gate 3 is pretty great right out of the box, but it could be argued that its second act lacks some variety. If you aren't endlessly dazzled by shadowy forests and J.K.
body: As always, modders have you covered. An ambitious mod for BG3, simply called " Baldur's Gate 3: Act Two Expansion " just released after "almost two years in development," according to modder SquallyDaBeanz. As the description states, the expansion implements a custom zone called The Chionthar Wilds—"a whole new region to experience that is similar in scope to the Act 1 Wilderness."

With the mod installed, you can start adventuring in the new region (ideally with a party that's around level 8 or higher) after wrapping up in the Shadow-Cursed Lands, or via a quickstart button that takes you straight to the new stuff with options for equipment and hirelings.

Once there, the mod packs in new creatures to fight in over 30 new encounters, over 70 new items to collect, as well as new quests, NPCs, and cutscenes. EXP in the new zones is "artificially reduced," so clearing all this custom stuff shouldn't completely invalidate Act 3's difficulty if you're doing a full playthrough.
points: Baldur's Gate 3 is pretty great right out of the box, but it could be argued that its second act lacks some variety.

articles.title: HoYoverse's Nodusfall might look like Elden Ring, but there's a promising dark fantasy action game here that took me by surprise
articles.summary: Nodusfall, aesthetically at least, is about as far from a typical HoYoverse game as you can get. Gone are the bright colours, cute creatures, and bountiful anime women.
body: I'll admit to being a little worried at the beginning of my preview after learning it would consist of two boss battles fought in groups of four. After all, the majority of my co-op experience comes from RuneScape, a 25-year-old MMORPG primarily played with a mouse, and nobody wants to let their team down.

But first came the character selection. There were four options available in my demo: two focused around melee combat, two ranged. Both combat styles offered one character with healing-focused abilities which I immediately discounted - too much responsibility. The archer with a mechanical arm though? Inflicting heavy damage from a distance while taking care of any nasty surprises was definitely something I could do. Decision made, it was time to discover how my chosen role would actually play out in battle.
points: Nodusfall, aesthetically at least, is about as far from a typical HoYoverse game as you can get.

articles.title: Japanese devs aren't facing the same layoff crisis because their executives are paid an order of magnitude less, 'they didn’t get swept up in the live-service trend,' and their teams are smaller, says industry expert
articles.summary: In an interview first published in Edge Magazine issue 428 and shared online via its Knowledge newsletter, former Tencent Games business development director and inaugural Game Awards Game Changer Amir Satvat offered his take on why the now-yearslong games industry layoff crisis has been so uneven…
body: There's been a lot of debate whether the past three years have matched the infamous '83 videogame crash⁠— Brenda Romero says yes, Tim Cain argues not quite (both saw it firsthand). "I think this is as bad as the '83 crash if you’re a game developer based in North America or Western Europe, in a traditional triple-A studio," said Satvat. "That is ground zero for the destruction." Satvat expanded on this particular observation in a recent post on LinkedIn.

"Japan is a completely different ballgame," Satvat said, praising its industry-wide tendency to retain staff, even if sacrifices are required in short-term profit or executive compensation. "Everyone calls out Nintendo, but you can look at Konami or Capcom⁠—these companies all have staff retention of 97%+."

"My understanding is that, generally, Japanese teams tend to be much smaller and leaner," Satvat added. "They didn’t get swept up in the live-service trend, or into these mega-blockbusters with 500-person teams." He also pointed to one of the great crazy-making contradictions of the ongoing crisis: "The executive salaries. [Japanese executives] still make great money, but it’s two or three million dollars, not 30 million."

articles.title: 'The largest theft of labor in human history:' Court docs reveal Microsoft exec predicted AI 'doom loops' could hollow out the internet
articles.summary: In Dec. 2023, The New York Times filed one of the biggest copyright lawsuits in recent memory against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging that its AI models heisted ludicrous amounts of journalistic work from the Times.
body: Perhaps the most shocking sentiments are from Microsoft's director of applied science, Brent Hecht, who wrote in an internal presentation that Copilot's answer engine would "hurt the performance of our models and the entire web at the same time."

Internal data from Microsoft suggests that the engine caused click-through rates for The New York Times search results to drop at rates between 87% to 93% compared to standard Bing searches. For Ziff Davis domains—the company that owns Eurogamer and IGN—click-through rates dropped between 51% and 94%.

The filing also reveals that when a researcher for OpenAI, Nick Ryder, told OpenAI president Greg Brockman about "a hack to get around nytimes paywall" to help scrape its writing, Brockman replied "ah nice." OpenAI internal documents see Brockman writing that LLMs are "very good at any news task."

articles.title: Indie Dev Says “AI” Voice In His Game Was Actually His Wife
articles.summary: Someone playing Refractive Entertainment's recently released action-RPG Luminary for less than an hour accused the team of using AI for the game's only voiced character. The player said the voice "killed it" for them. There was just one problem: It wasn't AI.
body: Refractive Entertainment launched Luminary into Steam Early Access on August 11. It's a resource-gathering action-adventure sandbox with an art style that's giving Fable meets Immortals Fenyx Rising. It's cute-looking and well-received, with a "Mostly Positive" rating out of almost 350 Steam reviews. But for an indie developer who says his game's success lives and dies by its Steam review score, one particular negative review caught the creative director's attention.

On September 10, user NyteKnyte posted a short Steam review after only 0.4 hours with the game to say that Luminary looked good but "the awful AI-generated voice killed it" for them. "Feels off, like an AI game," NyteKnyte said in their review. "Hopefully its temporary and gets better, but [the AI voice] killed it for me."
Not long after this review hit the game's Steam page, Refractive Entertainment responded, saying that the “awful AI-generated voice” that NyteKnyte decried was actually the creative director's wife.

videos.title: The Resident Evil Movie Understands Video Games Are Ridiculous, and That's Why It's Great
videos.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie understands that video games are ridiculous, and that's why it's great.
body: Video games are ridiculous. The Resident Evil series is a perfect example. One moment you’re running in terror from a comically oversized, trench-coated tank of a man in a tiny hat; the next, you’re messing around with electronic chess pieces to open a door. These are completely alien situations that, somehow, these games compel us to navigate with rational thought. This is what Zach Cregger understands so well about Capcom’s genre-defining series. His Resident Evil movie knows this is ridiculous, so it lets its lead, Brian, progress through a 90-minute rollercoaster just as we would with a controller in our hands. It’s a fantastic translation of the sensation of playing a survival horror game, never forgetting to include every piece of glorious nonsense that comes with it.
